hide_of_nemean_lion.name: Hide of the Nemean Lion
hide_of_nemean_lion.unidentified_name: a rough amber pelt of unnatural density
hide_of_nemean_lion.lore: The Nemean Lion's hide could not be cut by any weapon — that was the point of the first Labour. Heracles strangled it. The lion's own claws were the only things sharp enough to skin it. He wore the hide thereafter. Every subsequent monster he faced had to find a way to harm a man armoured in the unskinnable. Most didn't manage it. The hide renders its wearer virtually invulnerable to conventional weapons — only magical or divine arms can pierce it.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Hide of the Nemean Lion turns all but divine arms — armor class improves by 2.

carapace_of_the_hydra.name: Carapace of the Hydra
carapace_of_the_hydra.unidentified_name: a greenish scaled vest that smells faintly of venom
carapace_of_the_hydra.lore: Heracles used the Hydra's caustic blood to poison his arrows — the same arrows that killed Chiron by accident and Nessus by intention and started the chain that killed Heracles himself. The Hydra's outer scale was immune to its own venom. This is the standard configuration: weapons made from the thing they destroy are often proof against the same.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Carapace of the Hydra was immune to its own venom — it deflects 50% of incoming poison.

panoply_of_hephaestus.name: Panoply of Hephaestus
panoply_of_hephaestus.unidentified_name: a suit of armour of inhuman precision
panoply_of_hephaestus.lore: Hephaestus was thrown from Olympus by his mother (or his father, depending on which Homer you read) and landed on Lemnos. He survived, became the smith of the gods, and made the best things in existence: Achilles' armour, the golden automata that walked him to his forge, the chain-net that caught Aphrodite and Ares in bed, the bronze giant Talos. Everything he made was perfect. He himself walked with a limp.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Panoply of Hephaestus is a smith-god's masterwork — armor class improves by 2.

dragon_mail_of_sigurd.name: Dragon-Sewn Mail of Sigurd
dragon_mail_of_sigurd.unidentified_name: a shirt of scale-linked rings with a faint iridescence
dragon_mail_of_sigurd.lore: After killing Fafnir, Sigurd bathed in the dragon's blood and became invulnerable — except for a leaf that fell between his shoulder blades. His eventual murder came from a spear through exactly that spot, thrown by a man told about it by a woman who loved him and was told by another man who needed Sigurd dead. The weak point was the information, not the armour.

mastery_blessing.desc: Dragon-Sewn Mail of Sigurd grants +50% fire resistance.

breastplate_of_joan.name: Breastplate of Joan of Arc
breastplate_of_joan.lore: Joan of Arc described her armour as 'very good' — white-painted steel made specifically for her. She was wounded multiple times and fought on. She told her judges at her trial that her armour had been made by command of God and could not protect against what God willed. They burned her anyway. Twenty-five years later Charles VII had the verdict annulled. Joan had been dead for twenty-five years.

mastery_blessing.desc: Joan of Arc fought on through every wound — her breastplate grants a permanent 20 HP on mastery.

lorica_hamata_of_caesar.name: Lorica of Caesar
lorica_hamata_of_caesar.unidentified_name: a fine ring-mail shirt of late Republican make
lorica_hamata_of_caesar.lore: Julius Caesar wore chain-mail. He also reportedly wore a special hat to cover his baldness and was sensitive about being called a king by the Senate. He was stabbed twenty-three times. The physician Antistius found only one wound fatal. The other senators had been imprecise or hesitant. Caesar had refused his bodyguard. He had been warned. He understood warnings as challenges.

mastery_blessing.desc: Caesar wore the chain-mail across the Rubicon and the Senate floor — the Lorica grants a permanent 15 HP on mastery.

orichalcum_breastplate.name: Orichalcum Breastplate
orichalcum_breastplate.unidentified_name: a chest-piece of reddish-gold metal that vibrates faintly
orichalcum_breastplate.lore: Orichalcum was the metal of Atlantis — mentioned by Plato in the Critias as the most prized substance in the world after gold. Its appearance was flame-red. The Atlanteans mined it everywhere, then it vanished when Atlantis sank. Modern scholars identify it as brass or a copper-zinc alloy. The identification is probably correct. Plato's text does not describe its resonance, which the surviving piece still exhibits.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Orichalcum Breastplate still resonates with the lost metal of Atlantis — it deflects 20% of all elemental damage.

helm_of_hades.name: Helm of Darkness
helm_of_hades.unidentified_name: a helm that seems to absorb light around it
helm_of_hades.lore: The Helm of Hades was made by the Cyclopes in the same forging that made Poseidon's trident and Zeus's lightning. Perseus borrowed it to approach the Gorgons unseen. Hermes lent it to Athena during the Trojan War. It did not grant invisibility — it prevented perception. The distinction seems technical until you realize the Helm worked on gods. No one can look away from nothing.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Helm of Darkness prevents perception itself — armor class improves by 2.

helm_of_achilles.name: Helm of Achilles
helm_of_achilles.unidentified_name: a bronze helm with a tall horse-hair crest
helm_of_achilles.lore: Hephaestus forged Achilles' new armour when Patroclus died wearing the old set. The helmet had a crest of horse-hair and rang like a bell. Achilles wore it for the last weeks of his life. It was awarded after his death to Odysseus over Ajax — a decision based on rhetoric and political judgement, not martial merit. The armour was better than both arguments.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Helm of Achilles rang like a bell for the last weeks of his life — it grants a permanent 15 HP on mastery.

great_helm_of_galahad.name: Great Helm of Galahad
great_helm_of_galahad.unidentified_name: a white helm with a red cross on the cheek
great_helm_of_galahad.lore: Galahad arrived at Camelot with a plain white shield and no name. He sat in the Siege Perilous — the seat that killed anyone not pure enough — and nothing happened. He was the only knight who completed the Grail quest because he was the only one who had not already compromised himself. His father Lancelot came within inches of it. Lancelot's single lapse in virtue cost him the quest and gave the world Galahad. The Grail works through irony.

mastery_blessing.desc: Galahad's purity allowed him the Grail — his great helm deflects 40% of unholy damage.

vambraces_of_achilles.name: Vambraces of Achilles
vambraces_of_achilles.lore: Part of the panoply Hephaestus forged. The vambraces bore scenes of working men and women — farmers, shepherds, dancers — as though the smith god remembered that war is fought over ordinary lives. The warriors who wore them over centuries may not have understood the pictures. The pictures were not for them.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Vambraces of Achilles bear scenes of working lives — armor class improves by 1.

gauntlets_of_mars.name: Gauntlets of Mars
gauntlets_of_mars.lore: Mars was the second most worshipped god in Rome after Jupiter. Unlike Ares, his Greek equivalent, he was not merely the god of war but of agriculture and the protection of boundaries — the army that defends fields is the same army that works them. His priests carried sacred shields believed to have fallen from heaven and danced with them in procession every March. The month is named for him. So is Tuesday, through Tiwaz/Tyr.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Gauntlets of Mars defend boundaries and break them — they grant a permanent 15 HP on mastery.

greaves_of_hermes.name: Greaves of Hermes
greaves_of_hermes.unidentified_name: winged bronze greaves of incredible lightness
greaves_of_hermes.lore: Hermes' winged sandals — the Talaria — were given him by his father Zeus or possibly won in trade with Perseus or possibly always his. He carried the dead to Hades in them. Perseus borrowed them for the Medusa mission along with the Helm and Kibisis bag. The wings are the most depicted element of Hermes iconography, which is interesting because Hermes himself is most notable for what he carries between places, not the speed.

mastery_blessing.desc: Hermes's Greaves carried him between Olympus and Hades — armor class improves by 1.

cloak_of_the_morrigan.name: Cloak of the Morrigan
cloak_of_the_morrigan.unidentified_name: a dark feathered cloak that moves without wind
cloak_of_the_morrigan.lore: The Morrigan — the Phantom Queen — appeared as a crow or raven on the battlefield and chose who lived and died. She approached Cu Chulainn three times in disguise: as a young woman, an eel, a wolf, and a heifer. He rejected and fought each of them. Before his final battle she appeared as an old woman milking a lame cow, and he drank from her and was healed without knowing it. He died anyway. She had been kind to him; he had not recognized it.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Cloak of the Morrigan chooses who lives and dies — it deflects 30% of unholy damage.

leggings_of_enkidu.name: Leggings of Enkidu
leggings_of_enkidu.unidentified_name: rough-worked leather greaves from before metallurgy
leggings_of_enkidu.lore: Enkidu was created by the gods as a wild man to counter Gilgamesh. He lived among animals until a temple prostitute civilised him over seven days. He then challenged Gilgamesh to single combat; they fought to a draw and became friends. The Epic of Gilgamesh is the oldest known written epic. Its central subject is not the monsters they killed together but what Gilgamesh does when Enkidu dies first.

mastery_blessing.desc: Enkidu was made wild and made friend — his leggings grant a permanent 15 HP on mastery.

mantle_of_elijah.name: Mantle of Elijah
mantle_of_elijah.unidentified_name: a rough prophetic cloak of undyed wool
mantle_of_elijah.lore: Elijah's mantle passed to Elisha when Elijah was taken to heaven in a chariot of fire. Elisha used it to part the Jordan River on his return. In Jewish tradition it represents the transfer of prophetic authority — the mantle is the office, not the man. When Elijah threw it on Elisha's shoulders without asking, Elisha left his oxen and ran after him. He was ploughing when it happened. He finished the field first.

mastery_blessing.desc: Elijah was taken to heaven in a chariot of fire — his mantle deflects 30% of fire damage.

robe_of_the_magus.name: Robe of the Magus
robe_of_the_magus.unidentified_name: a deep blue robe with silver astronomical diagrams
robe_of_the_magus.lore: The Magi of the ancient Near East were not magicians in the popular sense — they were scholars of astronomy, dream interpretation, and the hidden correspondences between celestial and earthly events. The Star they followed was either a conjunction of Jupiter and Saturn, a comet, or a nova. They brought gold, frankincense, and myrrh and went home 'another way,' having been warned in a dream not to report back to Herod.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Robe of the Magus belonged to scholars who read the stars — it deflects 30% of psychic damage.

boots_of_seven_leagues.name: Boots of Seven Leagues
boots_of_seven_leagues.unidentified_name: a pair of worn leather boots that feel ready to move
boots_of_seven_leagues.lore: In European folklore, seven-league boots take their wearer seven leagues — about 35 km — per step. Hop-o'-My-Thumb stole them from an ogre. Puss in Boots wore them. They appear across French, German, and Scandinavian tales with minor variation: the boots are always disproportionately large on their original owner and always fit the hero perfectly. The folklore does not explain the sizing mechanism.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Boots of Seven Leagues fit their hero perfectly — armor class improves by 1.

brigandine_of_william_wallace.name: Brigandine of Wallace
brigandine_of_william_wallace.unidentified_name: a riveted coat of small iron plates over leather
brigandine_of_william_wallace.lore: William Wallace was not the painted barbarian of popular cinema. He was a second son of a minor noble family who became a guerrilla commander, won the Battle of Stirling Bridge by understanding terrain better than the English generals, was eventually captured, and was executed by a method the English used specifically to maximise dishonour. He gave no speech at his death. He denied nothing. The armour is real; the speeches were invented later.

mastery_blessing.desc: Wallace's brigandine carried him through Stirling Bridge — it grants a permanent 20 HP on mastery.

cuirass_of_hannibal.name: Cuirass of Hannibal
cuirass_of_hannibal.lore: Hannibal Barca crossed the Alps with war elephants in 218 BCE and fought Rome for sixteen years on its own soil. He won every major engagement: Trebia, Trasimene, Cannae — Cannae being the most studied battle in military history, used as a model for encirclement tactics by commanders for two millennia. He never took Rome. He was eventually called home to defend Carthage, lost one battle, and died in exile. He won the tactics and lost the war. Military academies still teach him.

mastery_blessing.desc: Hannibal won every major engagement in Italy — his cuirass grants a permanent 20 HP on mastery.

nemean_pelt.name: Nemean Lion Pelt
nemean_pelt.lore: The hide of the Nemean Lion, impossible to cut or pierce. Hercules used its own claws to skin it. Wearing it is like wearing the beast itself.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Nemean Pelt is the unskinnable hide itself — it deflects 25% of all elemental damage.

green_knights_plate.name: Green Knight's Plate
green_knights_plate.lore: Forged from enchanted iron that grows with the wearer, the Green Knight's Plate absorbs blows that would kill a lesser man. The wearer heals slowly but continuously.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Green Knight's Plate grows with its wearer — it grants a permanent 25 HP on mastery.

serpent_scale_mail.name: Serpent Scale Mail
serpent_scale_mail.lore: Scales from Jörmungandr's juvenile form, each harder than iron. The poison that suffuses them has been neutralized — but it still repels toxins entirely.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Serpent Scale Mail repels toxins entirely — it deflects 50% of poison damage.

arachne_silk_cloak.name: Arachne's Silk Cloak
arachne_silk_cloak.lore: Woven by Arachne before her transformation, this cloak is lighter than air and tougher than leather against piercing weapons. It catches arrows and slows blades.

mastery_blessing.desc: Arachne's Silk Cloak catches arrows and slows blades — armor class improves by 1.

erlking_mantle.name: Erlking's Mantle
erlking_mantle.lore: Woven from the living branches of the Erlking's forest, this cloak sharpens the senses of the wearer. Sound and sight carry further, and hidden things become easier to discern.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Erlking's Mantle sharpens every sense — it deflects 30% of psychic damage.

anansi_web_cloak.name: Anansi's Web Cloak
anansi_web_cloak.lore: Spun by Anansi himself from the thread of a thousand stories, this cloak shifts and deceives. Attacks that should land somehow miss. Traps somehow fail to trigger.

mastery_blessing.desc: Anansi's Web Cloak shifts and deceives — armor class improves by 2.

nidhoggr_scale.name: Níðhöggr's Scale
nidhoggr_scale.lore: A single scale from Níðhöggr's body, imbued with the rot of ages. Nothing corrodes it. Wearing it grants the wearer immunity to acid and strong resistance to all decay-based attacks.

mastery_blessing.desc: Níðhöggr's Scale resists all corrosion — it deflects 50% of acid damage.

aegishjalmr.name: Aegishjalmr
aegishjalmr.unidentified_name: a helm inscribed with a terrifying rune
aegishjalmr.lore: The Helm of Awe — ægishjálmr — is described in the Volsunga Saga and the Reginsmal of the Poetic Edda as the prize hoarded by the dragon Fafnir. He boasted of it on his deathbed: while he wore it, no man dared meet his eye. Sigurd took it after the killing, along with the gold and the cursed ring. Later Icelandic grimoires draw the helm as an eight-armed stave to be painted on the forehead in blood or spittle before a fight. It is less a helm than a sign worn on a helm.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Helm of Awe makes no man dare meet your eye — it deflects 30% of psychic damage.

winged_sandals_of_hermes.name: Winged Sandals of Hermes
winged_sandals_of_hermes.unidentified_name: sandals with small golden wings at the ankles
winged_sandals_of_hermes.lore: The talaria of Hermes, messenger of the gods, allowed him to fly between Olympus, Earth, and the Underworld in moments. Perseus borrowed them to approach Medusa. These sandals carry their wearer with divine swiftness — each step covers ground that would take mortals three.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Winged Sandals of Hermes carry you with divine swiftness — armor class improves by 2.

hermes_sandals_early.name: Hermes's Sandals
hermes_sandals_early.unidentified_name: a pair of sandals with tiny wing motifs
hermes_sandals_early.lore: Hermes's true talaria — described in the Iliad and the Homeric Hymn to Hermes — were golden and carried him on the wind between Olympus and the underworld. These are a mortal smith's copy, the kind hung on temple walls as a votive after a successful errand. The wings are bronze and the leather is good but ordinary. They carry only one trick from the god, and only briefly: enemies always seem to look the wrong way as you pass.

mastery_blessing.desc: These votive Hermes's Sandals carry one trick from the god — armor class improves by 1.

blindfold.name: blindfold
blindfold.lore: A strip of heavy black cloth. Wearing it plunges you into total darkness — you cannot see anything at all. A desperate measure, but sometimes not seeing is the only way to survive what lurks in the dark.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Blindfold severs sight from soul — it deflects 50% of psychic damage.

trainers_cap.name: Trainer's Cap
trainers_cap.lore: A well-worn red and white cap, its brim shaped by countless adventures. It radiates a warm, encouraging energy that invigorates companion creatures, helping them recover from wounds more quickly. The inside of the brim reads: 'I choose you.'

mastery_blessing.desc: The Trainer's Cap radiates encouragement and bond — it grants a permanent 10 HP on mastery.

cow_kings_horns.name: Cow King's Horns
cow_kings_horns.lore: The gilded horns of the Cow King, ripped from his crowned skull by a victorious adventurer. When worn, the horns channel bovine fury into every strike, granting a free chain hit before the quiz even begins — making it impossible to miss entirely. The left horn is inscribed with a single word: 'Moo.'

mastery_blessing.desc: The Cow King's Horns channel bovine fury — they grant a permanent 15 HP on mastery.

cloth_of_penelope.name: Cloth of Penelope
cloth_of_penelope.lore: Penelope, wife of Odysseus, waited twenty years for her husband's return from Troy. Each day she wove a funeral shroud; each night she unraveled it, buying time against the suitors who demanded she remarry. This cloth is woven from that same thread — thread that refused to stay finished, that healed itself every night. When worn, the wearer's wounds close slowly but surely, as if time itself is being unwoven.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Cloth of Penelope was woven and unwoven for twenty years — it grants a permanent 10 HP on mastery.

bracers_of_cu_chulainn.name: Bracers of Cu Chulainn
bracers_of_cu_chulainn.lore: Cu Chulainn, the Hound of Ulster, was Ireland's greatest warrior — a man who entered such battle frenzy that his body twisted and contorted, one eye bulging, his hair standing like spikes of flame. These bracers are stained with the blood of a hundred battles. They carry the warp-spasm's echo: the wearer strikes harder, bleeds enemies with every blow, and feels no pain from cuts.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Bracers of Cu Chulainn carry the warp-spasm — they grant a permanent 15 HP on mastery.

cloak_of_sun_wukong.name: Cloak of Sun Wukong
cloak_of_sun_wukong.lore: The Monkey King, Sun Wukong, was born from a stone egg on the Mountain of Flowers and Fruit. He stole the peaches of immortality, defied the Jade Emperor, and was imprisoned under a mountain for five hundred years before accompanying the monk Tripitaka westward. His seventy-two transformations made him impossible to pin down. This cloak carries that trickster spirit — the wearer seems to shimmer and shift, making them difficult to strike.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Cloak of Sun Wukong shimmers and shifts — armor class improves by 1.

coat_of_cu_chulainn.name: Coat of Cú Chulainn
coat_of_cu_chulainn.unidentified_name: a blood-red hide coat that pulses warmly
coat_of_cu_chulainn.lore: The war-harness of Cú Chulainn, the Hound of Ulster. When his blood was up, his body twisted into the ríastrad — the warp-spasm — and no army could stand before him. The coat remembers. When its wearer's life hangs by a thread, it awakens something primal: strength surges, pain fades, but the fury has a cost.

mastery_blessing.desc: +20 max HP while wearing the Coat of Cu Chulainn.

babr_e_bayan.name: Babr-e Bayan
babr_e_bayan.unidentified_name: a tiger-skin coat of impossible toughness
babr_e_bayan.lore: The tiger-skin armor of Rostam, greatest hero of the Shahnameh. He wore it through his Seven Labors — against the lion, the desert, the dragon, the witch, the demon Aulad, the Div-e Sepid, and the Div-e Akvan. The skin remembers every blow it absorbed. On each new floor, it will absorb the first strike completely, as though the blow never fell.

mastery_blessing.desc: Babr-e Bayan grants +20% resistance to all elemental damage.

tarnhelm.name: Tarnhelm
tarnhelm.unidentified_name: a dull iron helm that seems hard to look at
tarnhelm.lore: Forged by the Nibelung dwarf Mime for Alberich, who used it to enslave his own kin. Siegfried took it after slaying Fafnir. The Tarnhelm renders its wearer invisible — not merely hidden, but absent from perception entirely. Monsters lose all awareness of the wearer. The effect is brief, and the helm must recover its power between uses.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Tarnhelm renders its wearer absent from perception — armor class improves by 2.

linothorax_of_alexander.name: Linothorax of Alexander
linothorax_of_alexander.unidentified_name: a stiff cuirass of layered white linen
linothorax_of_alexander.lore: Alexander the Great wore linothorax — layers of linen glued and quilted into a stiff cuirass. It was lighter than bronze, cheaper to make, and stopped arrows. The Macedonian phalanx wore it. The Romans copied it. Modern reconstructions tested with bows confirmed: twenty layers of linen will turn an arrow that punches through wood.

mastery_blessing.desc: Alexander's Linothorax stops what punches through wood — armor class improves by 1.

coif_of_beowulf.name: Coif of Beowulf
coif_of_beowulf.unidentified_name: a riveted iron coif of Anglo-Saxon make
coif_of_beowulf.lore: Beowulf rode to Heorot and killed Grendel bare-handed because his sword would not bite the troll's hide. He kept the arm as a trophy. His coif, the poet says, was 'wound with wires by a weapon-smith of cunning' — the lines of the Sutton Hoo helmet match the description almost exactly. Archaeology caught up with the poem in 1939.

mastery_blessing.desc: Beowulf's coif was 'wound with wires by a weapon-smith of cunning' — it grants a permanent 10 HP on mastery.

sandals_of_perseus.name: Sandals of Perseus
sandals_of_perseus.unidentified_name: a worn pair of bronze-buckled sandals
sandals_of_perseus.lore: Before Perseus borrowed Hermes' winged talaria, he wore ordinary bronze-buckled sandals — the same Mycenaean style every shepherd and soldier wore. Athena visited him in those sandals. The gods gave him better gear later because the better gear was needed for Medusa, not because his own was inadequate. He kept the originals. The pair found at Lerna may or may not be his.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Sandals of Perseus walked the road to Medusa — armor class improves by 1.

kilt_of_the_pharaoh.name: Kilt of the Pharaoh
kilt_of_the_pharaoh.unidentified_name: a starched pleated linen kilt with gilt threads
kilt_of_the_pharaoh.lore: The shendyt was the kilt worn by Egyptian royalty for three thousand years — pleated linen, sometimes stiffened with starch, sometimes embroidered with gold thread. Tutankhamun was buried with several. The dry climate preserved the linen better than the wood of the coffins. A pharaoh's clothes outlasted his furniture.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Kilt of the Pharaoh is starched linen with the desert's defiance — it deflects 25% of fire damage.

scale_of_dilmun.name: Scale of Dilmun
scale_of_dilmun.unidentified_name: a bronze scale shirt of Mesopotamian make
scale_of_dilmun.lore: Dilmun was the Sumerian paradise — somewhere in the Persian Gulf, possibly Bahrain — where Enki and his wife lived without sickness or old age. Gilgamesh sought immortality there and found Utnapishtim, the flood survivor, instead. The scale armour found in Dilmun-era tombs predates the Hittite scale shirts by centuries. The Sumerians invented most things first.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Scale of Dilmun came from the Sumerian paradise — it grants a permanent 12 HP on mastery.

helm_of_gilgamesh.name: Helm of Gilgamesh
helm_of_gilgamesh.lore: The royal helmets found at Ur are made of beaten gold and electrum, light enough to wear but ornamental enough that a real fight would dent them out of shape. They were buried with the king. Gilgamesh was a real king of Uruk — the tablets list him — and the epic about him was already old when scribes copied it in the second millennium BCE. The story is older than the script that records it.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Helm of Gilgamesh remembers Uruk's king — it grants a permanent 12 HP on mastery.

sandals_of_theseus.name: Sandals of Theseus
sandals_of_theseus.unidentified_name: weathered leather sandals with bronze studs
sandals_of_theseus.lore: Aegeus left his sandals and sword under a rock outside Troezen. When Theseus was old enough to lift the rock, he took both and walked to Athens. The road was infested with bandits. He killed Sinis, Sciron, and Procrustes by their own methods. The sandals walked through every Labour of the Athenian cycle. Athens kept them in the temple of Theseus until the Persians burned it.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Sandals of Theseus walked from Troezen through every Labour — armor class improves by 1.

greaves_of_qin.name: Greaves of the Qin Guard
greaves_of_qin.unidentified_name: lacquered leather greaves stamped with seal-script
greaves_of_qin.lore: Qin Shi Huangdi's Terracotta Army was eight thousand soldiers in full kit, buried with the first emperor in 210 BCE. Every figure is individual — different face, different armour, different rank. The leg armour on the standing infantry is lacquered leather scales laced with cord. Lacquer waterproofs leather and stiffens it. The Qin engineers understood materials science.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Greaves of the Qin Guard are lacquered to resist water and weather — armor class improves by 1.

cloak_of_odin.name: Wanderer's Cloak of Odin
cloak_of_odin.unidentified_name: a deep blue traveler's cloak with one missing eyelet
cloak_of_odin.lore: Odin disguised himself as a one-eyed wanderer in a wide-brimmed hat and a blue cloak. He visited halls, drank with mortals, set them riddles, and left without saying who he was. Half the saga heroes have an encounter with a strange old man at a turning point — the old man is always Odin. He came to find out what humans were doing. He never quite trusted his own answer.

mastery_blessing.desc: Odin walked among men in this cloak and set them riddles — it deflects 30% of psychic damage.

bracers_of_arjuna.name: Bracers of Arjuna
bracers_of_arjuna.unidentified_name: engraved leather bracers with brass studs
bracers_of_arjuna.lore: Arjuna was the third of the Pandava brothers and the greatest archer of the Mahabharata. Before Kurukshetra, his charioteer Krishna delivered the Bhagavad Gita over eighteen chapters while the armies waited. Arjuna had wanted to lay down his bow. By the end of the song he understood why he could not. He fought. The Gita is the oldest battlefield-philosophy text we have.

mastery_blessing.desc: Arjuna's Bracers held the bow through Kurukshetra — armor class improves by 1.

girdle_of_hippolyta.name: Girdle of Hippolyta
girdle_of_hippolyta.unidentified_name: a braided leather war-girdle with a bronze clasp
girdle_of_hippolyta.lore: Hippolyta, queen of the Amazons, owned a war-girdle given her by Ares. Heracles' ninth Labour was to take it. She offered it freely; Hera disguised herself as an Amazon and started a rumor that he was kidnapping the queen. The Amazons attacked. Heracles killed Hippolyta and took the girdle. The story has variants — in some, Hippolyta lives and the girdle is paid for. The variants reflect later discomfort with the source.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Girdle of Hippolyta was Ares's gift to the Amazon queen — STR rises by 2 permanently.

helm_of_leonidas.name: Helm of Leonidas
helm_of_leonidas.unidentified_name: a Corinthian bronze helm with a transverse crest
helm_of_leonidas.lore: Leonidas of Sparta held Thermopylae against Xerxes' army with three hundred Spartans and a few thousand allies. He died on the third day. Spartan helmets had a transverse crest — a horsehair brush running ear to ear — that marked officers. Persians who saw the Spartans combing their hair on the morning of the last battle reported it as strange. The Spartans were preparing for death the way their custom required.

mastery_blessing.desc: Leonidas's transverse-crested helm held the pass for three days — it grants a permanent 20 HP on mastery.

cloak_of_mulan.name: Cloak of Mulan
cloak_of_mulan.unidentified_name: a heavy red wool cloak with frost-line patterns
cloak_of_mulan.lore: Hua Mulan took her father's place in the army of the Northern Wei. The Ballad of Mulan is from the sixth century and uses sixty-two lines to cover twelve years of war. She came home, changed into a dress, and her comrades did not recognize her. The poem treats her gender disguise as the smallest of her accomplishments. The army-life details are correct enough that historians use the ballad as source material.

mastery_blessing.desc: Mulan's Cloak hid her in plain sight for twelve years of war — armor class improves by 2.

haramaki_of_yoshitsune.name: Haramaki of Yoshitsune
haramaki_of_yoshitsune.unidentified_name: a deep red lacquer-laced cuirass of small plates
haramaki_of_yoshitsune.lore: Minamoto no Yoshitsune was the great general of the Genpei War. He won the battles of Ichi-no-Tani and Dan-no-ura by cavalry tactics nobody on either side expected. His older brother Yoritomo, who founded the shogunate, turned on him afterward and hunted him to his death. Yoshitsune's loyalty to family was repaid the way loyalty often is in court politics. The samurai class spent the next eight centuries reading the story.

mastery_blessing.desc: Yoshitsune's haramaki carried him through Ichi-no-Tani and Dan-no-ura — it grants a permanent 20 HP on mastery.

boots_of_thor.name: Iron Boots of Thor
boots_of_thor.unidentified_name: heavy iron boots scarred by lightning
boots_of_thor.lore: Thor wore iron gloves to hold Mjolnir without crushing his fingers, a belt of strength that doubled his power, and iron boots for the same reason wrestlers chalk their hands. The Eddas list the three together as his ordinary kit — not the legendary parts of his story, just what he wore to work. The gear was practical. The thunder came from the work he did in it.

mastery_blessing.desc: Thor's iron boots are his ordinary working kit — they grant a permanent 20 HP on mastery.

helm_of_aragorn.name: Helm of the King Returned
helm_of_aragorn.unidentified_name: a winged silver helm with a pale gem in the brow
helm_of_aragorn.lore: Aragorn son of Arathorn was raised in Rivendell because his father had been killed and the line of Isildur could not be allowed to die in the wild. He went by Strider for most of his life. He earned the helm by going north when going north was the work nobody wanted. Tolkien's central argument — that the willing exile is the rightful king — is older than the book. The Britons told it about Arthur. The Israelites told it about David.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Helm of the King Returned carries the line of Isildur — it deflects 35% of unholy damage.

robes_of_solomon.name: Robes of Solomon
robes_of_solomon.unidentified_name: robes of gold thread embroidered with seventy-two names
robes_of_solomon.lore: Solomon's wisdom was the gift he asked for when God offered him anything. The wealth and the long reign came as a bonus. Late tradition gave him a signet ring that commanded the demons; the embroidered names on his robes were said to be theirs. The Temple he built was destroyed twice. The Wisdom literature attributed to him survives. The robes are what wisdom looks like when it has been embroidered for the throne room.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Robes of Solomon are embroidered with the names of bound demons — they deflect 40% of psychic damage.

armor_of_ragnarok.name: Armor of Ragnarök
armor_of_ragnarok.unidentified_name: an iron-and-bone harness scarred by old burns
armor_of_ragnarok.lore: Ragnarök is the doom of the gods. Odin dies in the wolf's mouth. Thor kills the world-serpent and walks nine steps before falling from its venom. The world burns and sinks and rises again with a smaller pantheon and a memory of what happened. This is the harness for the day the gods knew was coming and went out to meet anyway. The Norse called that courage, not despair.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Armor of Ragnarök is the harness for the day the gods went out to meet anyway — it grants a permanent 25 HP on mastery.

crown_of_brahma.name: Crown of Brahma
crown_of_brahma.unidentified_name: a four-tiered golden crown that hums with mantra
crown_of_brahma.lore: Brahma is the creator, the first of the Trimurti. He has four faces because he looked in every direction at once when his consort Saraswati was created and could not stop looking. The crown he wears is unrelated to any earthly metal. The Mahabharata says he gave it to a king who returned it. The king's name is not recorded. Some gifts are too large to keep.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Crown of Brahma was the creator's own — it deflects 30% of all elemental damage.

duck_of_doom.name: Duck of Doom
duck_of_doom.lore: You should know better than to pick up a duck in a dungeon.

mastery_blessing.desc: The Duck of Doom has no master!
